pr.title: gh-128133: Added relaxed atomics to bytes_hash

review_comments.body:
Please use `_Py_COMP_DIAG_PUSH` && `_Py_COMP_DIAG_IGNORE_DEPR_DECLS` && `_Py_COMP_DIAG_POP` to silence the warning.

Example of usage:
```c
static inline void
set_ob_shash(PyBytesObject *a, Py_hash_t hash)
{
_Py_COMP_DIAG_PUSH
_Py_COMP_DIAG_IGNORE_DEPR_DECLS
#ifdef Py_GIL_DISABLED
    _Py_atomic_store_int_relaxed((int *)&a->ob_shash, (int)hash);
#else
    a->ob_shash = hash;
#endif
_Py_COMP_DIAG_POP
}
Thanks! Fixed as per your suggestions. But the pipeline still seems to be failing with `_Py_hashtable_set: Assertion entry == NULL' failed.`
You can remove `_Py_COMP_DIAG_PUSH` etc from callers now.
A `Py_hash_t` is (generally?) an ssize, not an int. We should be using `_Py_atomic_store_ssize_relaxed`.
We aren't using any of the FT wrappers, this should just the `pycore_atomic` header.
This should be `get_ob_shash()` again to catch when the value was just set.

See @ZeroIntensity's comment above: 

> A Py_hash_t is (generally?) an ssize, not an int. We should be using _Py_atomic_store_ssize_relaxed.

https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/128412/files#r1900983357

https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/hash.html#c.Py_hash_t

This doc says signed int. Would happy to change if you confirm it is ssize though
The docs are using "integer" to generically mean an integer type, not specifically the C `int` data type.

For reference, here is where `Py_hash_t` is defined as a typedef of `Py_ssize_t`:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/a626f9a67b76e5fe69677afd5f8317d8c61de8de/Include/pyport.h#L159
Hey, from what I see pycore_atomic file has been removed.

You can just return hash here directly.
```suggestion
    return hash;
```

> This should be `get_ob_shash()` again to catch when the value was just set.

Going off @ZeroIntensity review here. I think using the getter here makes more sense. My understanding for using the `get_ob_shash(a)` is that the getter ensures `ob_shash` isn't changed while it is being read. Please let me know if it is otherwise.

I think returning `hash` like @kumaraditya303 suggests makes sense here.

> My understanding for using the get_ob_shash(a) is that the getter ensures ob_shash isn't changed while it is being read.

Not exactly. Atomics loads with `memory_order_relaxed` that we use here basically achieve two things:

1) The load is atomic (i.e., a single indivisible operation). In particular, the compiler is not going to load parts of the field separately and then combine it. (In practice, that would be unlikely to happen anyways.)
2) The main thing is that it avoids undefined behavior. The language declares that data races, such as concurrent reads and writes, are undefined behavior. However, concurrent reads and writes that use atomics are not undefined behavior. So that means that thread sanitizer won't issue warnings here.

Thanks, Appreciate the detailed explanation! 

Question isn't the return non atomic though? Is that case we should worry about?
You don't need to worry about the `return`. Atomics only matter for loads and stores -- things like reading and writing variables. They're not applicable to the `return` keyword.

Ah yeah, I missed the `hash` reassignment in my original review, my bad. I thought that `hash` was loaded atomically, checked for `-1`, and then *only* the underlying `ob_shash` was atomically stored with a new value, leaving `hash` with the old value. Kumar's approach is more correct.
Thanks, for the explanations. Appreciate it

issue_comments.body: @kumaraditya303 can this get a backport to 3.13? It looks like PyO3 reliably hits a race in the bytes hash on module import. https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3/issues/4904#issuecomment-2652214787

Thanks @abhijeetsharma200 for the PR, and @kumaraditya303 for merging it 🌮🎉.. I'm working now to backport this PR to: 3.13.
🐍🍒⛏🤖
